newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia temple tourists evacuation by helicopter.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia temple tourists evacuation by helicopter.

text.p: Some 200 tourists and aid workers trapped by factional fighting in the north Cambodian tourist town of Siem Reap were being evacuated to Phnom Penh by helicopter, a military official said on Tuesday.
Earlier plans to evacuate the foreigners to the Thai border by road were abandoned after overnight clashes near the town between forces loyal to Cambodia's rival prime ministers.
"The helicopter has landed already and passengers are getting on," a military official at the town's airport told Reuters by telephone.

The official said there was overnight fighting about 20 km (13 miles) from the town between troops of the powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen and those loyal to ousted First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
The fighting broke out on the road from Siem Reap to Sisophon, he said, referring to the northwestern town near the Thai border.
The military official, loyal to Hun Sen, said that there was another clash at the outskirts of Siem Reap early on Tuesday as Hun Sen's troops tried to confiscate weapons from Ranariddh's men.
A Western source in the town said a Hun Sen military official told him that five of Hun Sen's men were wounded in the fighting and the road to Thailand had been mined.

Most of the tourists in the town, stranded after the closure of Phnom Penh's airport on Saturday due to fighting in the capital were confused and nervous, another westerner said from the town which is near the fabled Angkor Wat complex.
"Most people don't have a clue what's going on. There are a lot of nervous looks on people's faces," said Michael Hayes, a publisher of the Phnom Penh Post newspaper.
"The U.N. is collecting people all over town. They are trying to coordinate things," he said by telephone from the town.
Siem Reap was under the control of Hun Sen's forces while much of the surrounding countryside was controlled by Ranariddh's men.
Phnom Penh's international airport has been closed since Saturday morning because of the fighting.
